items.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

ctx.x: That reminds me of some stories I’ve heard about Basie. When arrangers would come in with their thing and he’d say, “Well this is good but—”
Well “Li’l Darlin’” was fast, and they played and Basie suggested playing it real slow, one-two-three-four. Biggest hit they ever had. Neal Hefti wrote it.
Can you imagine Neal Hefti going, now what are you doing? That slow?
